skill.name: flow-nexus-swarm
skill.description: Cloud-based AI swarm deployment and event-driven workflow automation with Flow Nexus.
skill.summary: Deploy and coordinate Flow Nexus AI swarms, agents, workflows, templates, and monitoring from AI coding tools.
skill.author: ruvnet

security_audit.summary: Most static detections are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline code, and documented MCP call examples. Confirmed risk remains in bash setup sections that run mutable npm or npx packages and register an MCP server. No prompt injection or malicious exfiltration intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Mutable npm and npx package execution
remediation.suggestion: Pin exact package versions, avoid @latest and @alpha in install examples, and document package verification steps.

remediation.issue: MCP server registration from an external command
remediation.suggestion: Describe required MCP permissions and require users to review the command before adding the server.

remediation.issue: Cloud orchestration data boundary is not documented
remediation.suggestion: Document what task data, files, metrics, and audit details may be sent to Flow Nexus.

content.value_statement: Complex agent work is hard to coordinate across tasks, tools, and deployment steps. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Flow Nexus swarm and workflow operations.
actual_capabilities: Initializes Flow Nexus swarms with hierarchical, mesh, ring, or star topology guidance.
Shows how to spawn researcher, coder, analyst, optimizer, and coordinator agents.
Defines event-driven workflows with steps, dependencies, triggers, retries, and priorities.
Explains monitoring for swarms, workflows, queues, audit trails, streams, and generated files.
Documents template-based swarm creation for development, research, DevOps, and enterprise workflows.
Provides setup steps for installing Flow Nexus and adding its MCP server to Claude Code.
limitations: Requires a Flow Nexus account, network access, and MCP tooling before examples can run.
The skill is guidance only and does not include executable source files.
Cloud workflow behavior depends on the Flow Nexus platform and configured permissions.
Setup examples use mutable npm package tags that should be pinned for production use.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Feature Delivery
use_cases.description: Plan backend, frontend, database, integration, and testing work across specialized agents.

use_cases.title: Automate Deployment Workflows
use_cases.description: Model CI, build, scan, staging, smoke test, and production deployment steps with dependencies.

use_cases.title: Run Parallel Research
use_cases.description: Use mesh swarms to divide research, compare findings, and synthesize results faster.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Starter Swarm
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a simple project
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Flow Nexus swarm skill to design a small star topology swarm for my project. Include agent roles and the first task.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Workflow Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Flow Nexus workflow for testing, building, security scanning, and staging deployment. Include dependencies and retry guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Select a Swarm Template
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend a Flow Nexus swarm template for a multi-repository code review project. Explain overrides for agent count and strategy.

prompt_templates.title: Design Multi-Swarm Coordination
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a multi-swarm Flow Nexus plan for research, implementation, testing, and release. Include monitoring and cleanup checkpoints.

output_examples.input: Plan a full-stack development swarm for an e-commerce project.
output_examples.output: A hierarchical swarm with coordinator, backend, frontend, database, and QA agents, plus a workflow from requirements through integration testing.

output_examples.input: Create a deployment workflow with safety checks.
output_examples.output: A staged workflow that runs linting, unit tests, integration tests, build, security scan, staging deploy, smoke tests, and production deploy.
A monitoring plan that checks workflow status, queue depth, audit trail entries, execution stream status, and cleanup actions.

best_practices: Choose topology based on coordination style, not agent count alone.
Use dependencies, retries, and timeouts for workflows that affect deployment or production data.
Destroy unused swarms and review audit trails after each major execution.
anti_patterns: Do not run mutable npm or npx setup commands without version pinning and source review.
Do not give cloud swarms broad production access before testing workflow behavior.
Do not use parallel execution for tasks that have hidden ordering or data dependencies.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps plan and operate Flow Nexus swarms, agents, workflows, templates, monitoring, and setup steps.

faq.question: Does it require Flow Nexus?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples assume Flow Nexus access, an account, network connectivity, and the Flow Nexus MCP server.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes MCP setup guidance for Claude Code and is also listed for Claude and Codex.

faq.question: Does it execute workflows by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides instructions and examples. Actual execution depends on configured Flow Nexus tools and permissions.

faq.question: What should I review before production use?
faq.answer: Review package versions, MCP server permissions, cloud credentials, workflow actions, and data sent to Flow Nexus.

faq.question: Is it only for software teams?
faq.answer: No. It also describes research, data processing, compliance review, incident response, and multi-repository coordination patterns.
